news.title: Moved my 354 GB from Google Photos to Proton Photos a few weeks ago - but I lost the one t…
news.author: mmornati@techhub.social
news.snippet: Moved my 354 GB from Google Photos to Proton Photos a few weeks ago - but I lost the one thing I took for granted: search. Proton Photos is end-to-end encrypted. Proton literally cannot see your photos, so it cannot index them. Any decent search engine has to run on your own hardware. That's what I built: proton-faces. 🎬 Demo: https:// res.cloudinary.com/blog-mornat i-net/video/upload/v1788111273/aqarlh1taqbygcsode6o.mp4 📖 Blog post: https:// blog.mornati.net/proton-faces- search-proton-photos/ 🔗 Repo: https:// github.com/mmornati/proton-fac es How it works: • Two containers. proton-bridge is the only component that ever talks to Proton (auth, timeline diff, 512px thumbnails, full-res on demand). The app does all the machine learning, indexing and search — and never sees a Proton credential. • Objects & scenes: CLIP ViT-B-32 via ONNX, CPU-only. Type "dog", "beach", "car" — zero-shot, no training needed. • Faces: InsightFace (RetinaFace + ArcFace), clustered into people with HDBSCAN. Name a person once, similar faces get auto-tagged. • Places: GPS comes from Google Takeout sidecars, matched by content hash (no full download), reverse-geocoded fully offline. The Places tab pins everything on an OpenStreetMap map. • Nothing is ever written back to Proton. No telemetry. Models are baked into the Docker image. ~1–2 s per photo, 100k photos in about a day, fully resumable. This is the sequel to my gphoto2proton migration post. MIT licensed, self-hosted, and the search bar finally works again — without giving Google my photos back. # ProtonPhotos # Privacy # SelfHosted # OpenSource # MachineLearning # CLIP # FOSS # Docker
